proposals.before: Hence Chang Fu's long bow to the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;
proposals.after: Hence the long bow to the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;
proposals.reason: Chinese 長揖楚相 is an allusion (“long bow to the Chu minister”); it does not name a person “Chang Fu.”

proposals.before: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Di, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!
proposals.after: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!
proposals.reason: Chinese 覽父綍 is Fu (綍), not Di; the given name was mistranslated.

proposals.before: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Di, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!
proposals.after: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!
proposals.reason: Chinese 覽父綍 is Fu (綍), not Di.

proposals.before: A messenger from the palace guard staff officer Wang Guo was again sent to convey the edict with earnest persuasion.
proposals.after: Palace guard staff officer Wang Guo was again sent to convey the edict with earnest persuasion.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遣領軍司馬王果 means Wang Guo himself was sent; the literal invents an extra messenger.

decisions.reason: s0055 長揖楚相 is an allusion to long-bowing to the Chu chancellor; 長揖 is not a personal name, so “Chang Fu” is invented and the proposed literal correctly removes it.
s0122 覽父綍 names Lan’s father as 綍 (Fu); “Di” is a mistranslation, and the proposed idiomatic restores the correct given name.
s0122 覽父綍 is Fu (綍), not Di; the proposed literal matches the Chinese personal name.
s0088 遣領軍司馬王果宣旨敦譬 has Wang Guo himself as the person sent to proclaim the edict; the before invents an intervening messenger, and the proposed literal removes that error.
